product_brief: Standalone OpenSSL 3 provider enabling liboqs-based quantum-safe and hybrid key exchange for TLS 1.3 and certificate operations.

product_brief: An efficient post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism (KEM) based on Module-LWE and Module-LWR lattice problems.
pqc_capability_description: SMAUG-T is a post-quantum KEM based on Module-LWE (MLWE) and Module-LWR (MLWR). It uses the Fujisaki-Okamoto transform for quantum security in the QROM. It includes a parameter set TiMER targeting security level 1. Reference implementation version 1.2.0 is available.
crypto_primitives: Module-Learning-with-Errors (MLWE), Module Learning-with-Roundings (MLWR), SHA256
implementation_attack_surface: Timing-Secure; constant-time implementation mentioned in v2.0 history; decryption failure probability (DFP) addressed via D2 encoding in TiMER.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: TiMER parameter set targets security level 1 with lower decryption failure probability; described as "Tiny sMaug".

product_brief: A module lattice-based signature scheme for shorter and easily maskable signatures, targeting space-limited scenarios like DNSSEC.
pqc_capability_description: HAETAE is a module lattice-based signature scheme based on the Fiat-Shamir with Aborts paradigm. It guarantees quantum security in the QROM. It uses bimodal distribution for rejection sampling and uniform distributions over hyperballs. It focuses on reducing signature and verification key sizes.
crypto_primitives: Module lattice-based signature scheme, Fiat-Shamir with Aborts, SHA256
implementation_attack_surface: The text states that discrete Gaussian distributions used in BLISS are SCA-vulnerable, and HAETAE uses uniform distributions over hyperballs instead. It mentions "easily maskable signatures."
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: The design targets space-limited scenarios such as DNSSEC, aiming for signatures that fit into one TCP or UDP datagram.

product_brief: A post-quantum signature scheme based on a zero-knowledge proof of preimage knowledge for a symmetric one-way function.
pqc_capability_description: AIMer is a signature scheme designed to be secure against quantum attacks, relying on the security of underlying symmetric primitives (AIM2). It uses the MPC-in-the-Head paradigm and BN++ proof system. It is a reference implementation for a PQC signature algorithm.
crypto_primitives: AIM2 (symmetric primitive), Hash functions, Extendable-output functions, BN++ proof system, MPC-in-the-Head
implementation_attack_surface: The document discusses security against algebraic attacks, brute-force attacks, differential and linear cryptanalysis, and quantum attacks on the AIM2 primitive. It mentions side-channel attacks in the table of contents but does not provide specific implementation vulnerability details in the provided text.

product_brief: Reference and optimized implementations of the NTRU+ post-quantum cryptographic scheme, including KEM and PKE variants.
pqc_capability_description: Provides reference and optimized implementations of NTRU+ KEM and PKE (specifically NTRU+{KEM,PKE}864). Version 2.2.1 includes revised specifications, corrected NTT layer counts, adjusted Lazy Barrett Reduction placement, and replaced Barrett with Montgomery reduction in optimized builds for performance.
crypto_primitives: NTRU+

product_brief: A lattice-based post-quantum cryptographic signature algorithm reference implementation designed for security against quantum computers.
pqc_support: Yes (Falcon is a post-quantum cryptographic signature algorithm submitted to NIST PQC Project)
pqc_capability_description: Falcon is a lattice-based signature scheme based on NTRU lattices and the short integer solution (SIS) problem. It uses "fast Fourier sampling" for speed and compactness. It is a reference implementation submitted to the NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography Project. It offers security against quantum computers, with variants Falcon-512 and Falcon-1024.

primary_platforms: Common desktop computer (Intel Core i5-8259U mentioned for benchmarks), small, memory-constrained embedded devices

pqc_roadmap_details: Round 3 candidate in NIST's Additional Digital Signatures process. Round 3 tweaks due to NIST by 14 August 2026. Next conference in first half of 2027.
